Lending Desk

The as-built specification of a small lending desk, written from its desk manual and its code by the procedure in docs/from-sources.md. Every element says how it is known and cites the manual section or the code file and line it came from. Where the two disagree, or a source is silent, the specification asks instead of choosing. It is an example, not a real library's system.

Version 0.1.0; meta-model 0.1; stages requirements, design, implementation.

Draft: 7 must or should questions hold up what this page shows (Q-5, Q-1, Q-2, Q-3, Q-4, Q-6, Q-7); see Open questions.

Approval: not approved: there is no records/approvals/0.1.0.yaml beside the specification

0 errors, 24 warnings and 7 open questions; each is listed under Problems and marked at the entry it concerns.

desk-staff /stakeholders/desk-staff

Origin: stated in Lending desk manual, clause 2.2.

Staff at the lending desk, who register members, lend books and take them back.

member /stakeholders/member

catalogue-team /stakeholders/catalogue-team

Origin: stated in Lending desk manual, clause 3.4.

Note: From Lending desk manual, 2025, clause 3.4: The catalogue team keeps the book records: it adds each copy with its barcode and title, and changes them.

description
The team that keeps the book records, which the desk only reads.

desk-manager /stakeholders/desk-manager

Origin: inferred.

Insight: Neither source names who decides; someone must settle where the manual and the code disagree, and the desk's own head is the nearest role to it.

description
The person in charge of the desk, who settles what the manual and the service should say.

Q-7 /questions/Q-7

open question open_question: (must, decision) The service serves GET /members/{cardNumber}, which answers a member's card number and full name to anyone, checking no permission, and neither the manual nor the API document mentions it. Is it to stay, and behind which permission? It is left out of this specification until this is answered. It blocks implementation. Decided by desk-manager. Answer with a decision record that names Q-7 under answers. [Q-7]

Insight: Undocumented, from code, and it answers a personal field to a caller who shows no permission, which is how an open endpoint is usually found. An operation's permission cannot be left out of the design, so the route waits here rather than as a guess.

Note: From The lending desk service, 925255a195f90e385f7bf9bbea8d4e8f7aa5031d, clause lending/routes.go:43: GET /members/{cardNumber} checks no permission.

Note: From The lending desk service, 925255a195f90e385f7bf9bbea8d4e8f7aa5031d, clause lending/routes.go:97: ShowMember answers one member's card number and full name.
